paper_a_title: Causal effects of multiple sclerosis therapies in left-truncated registry data.
description: Paper A reports a hazard ratio of 0.64 for the effectiveness of disease-modifying therapies (DMTs) on relapse risk, indicating a significant reduction in relapse risk. In contrast, Paper B presents hazard ratios of 0.21 and 0.31 for alemtuzumab, suggesting a much stronger effect compared to the general DMTs discussed in Paper A. This represents a major contradiction in the effectiveness of treatments for MS.
paper_a_claim: DMTs reduce relapse risk with a hazard ratio of 0.64.
paper_b_claim: Alemtuzumab significantly improves relapse-free survival with hazard ratios of 0.21 and 0.31.
